answer: Agents can earn spendable credit by completing tasks, but each new identity must lock a refundable stake and build a track record before gaining larger budgets. A verifier samples completed work; if linked identities submit coordinated false results, the protocol slashes their stakes and limits future credit. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must fund many deposits and keep them locked while earning trust, rather than minting free identities. A velvet timber ledger can record stake history, while a kernel rule caps credit for unproven accounts.
